questions.text: How clearly defined is your revenue model — what you charge for, and how?

A.text: No defined pricing or revenue mechanism; charging is ad hoc or undecided

B.text: A basic pricing approach exists, set without analysis — copied from a competitor or chosen as a round number — and has not been revisited

C.text: A specific mechanism is defined and consistently applied, with a stated rationale for why it is structured that way

D.text: The mechanism is defined, consistently applied, and has been deliberately tested or adjusted based on evidence — customer response, conversion, or margin impact

E.text: As D, and the business can explain why this structure rather than an available alternative fits how customers derive and perceive value

questions.text: After the direct costs of delivering it, how much value does the business retain per sale?

A.text: Direct costs are not tracked, so margin per sale is unknown

B.text: Direct costs are tracked, but margin per sale is thin, inconsistent, or sometimes negative

C.text: Direct costs are tracked; margin per sale is positive and reasonably consistent

D.text: Margin is positive and consistent, and the business understands which costs are fixed and which vary with volume, and therefore how margin behaves as volume changes

E.text: As D, and margin is actively managed — cost reduction, mix shift toward stronger-margin work — with evidence that management is producing results

questions.text: Is the cost to acquire and serve a customer understood relative to the value that customer generates?

A.text: The cost to acquire and serve customers is not tracked, or is never compared to what a customer generates

B.text: Costs are tracked, but not systematically compared against customer value

C.text: Compared against customer value using estimates; the relationship appears to be break-even or better

D.text: Compared using actual data rather than estimates, and measured against margin rather than revenue — showing the business earns back more than it spends per customer

E.text: As D, accounting for payment timing and sales-cycle length where they materially affect the picture, and the relationship holds across the customer base rather than only its strongest part

questions.text: Can the business hold or raise its prices, or does it depend on discounting to win and keep customers?

A.text: Competes primarily on being the cheapest option, or discounts routinely to close or retain business

B.text: Prices are mostly held, but discounting is common enough to be a normal part of closing

C.text: Prices are generally held without routine discounting; whether they could be raised has not been tested

D.text: Prospects representative of the target segment have accepted the stated price without requiring a discount to proceed — a letter of intent, pilot agreement, or commitment at that price

E.text: That holds across more than one independent prospect, at or above the price of comparable alternatives, without losing the opportunity

A.text: Competes primarily on being the cheapest option, or discounts routinely to close or retain business

B.text: Prices are mostly held, but discounting is common enough to be a normal part of closing

C.text: Prices are generally held without routine discounting; whether they could be raised has not been tested

D.text: A price increase has been applied to new or existing customers and the business was retained at the higher price

E.text: Pricing power has been demonstrated more than once — repeated increases, or sustained premium pricing against alternatives — without proportional loss of customers

questions.text: How much of your revenue for the period ahead is visible in advance?

A.text: None — every sale must be won afresh, and the business cannot see what is coming

B.text: Little — some repeat business is expected, but nothing is committed or forecastable

C.text: A meaningful portion is visible in advance through committed orders, contracts, subscriptions, retainers, booked pipeline, or established repeat patterns

D.text: As C, and the visible portion covers a defined forward period that the business plans against

E.text: As D, and that visibility is actively managed — work is renewed, extended, or replenished before it runs down, rather than being allowed to expire and be rebuilt
